name: Crossover
tagline: Near-scrap bitcoin rigs as a hash-paying e-boiler for Dutch greenhouses, dispatched by band against all-in power cost.
summary: Crossover sells heat-as-a-service to Westland greenhouse growers, who already trade power every quarter-hour with CHP, boilers and heat buffers. It owns immersion-cooled, near-scrap post-halving ASICs on a non-firm grid connection behind the grower's meter, valued as options on hashprice rather than by efficiency. A rolling 15-minute MILP co-dispatches the ASICs, boiler, buffer and CHP against all-in delivered power cost (EPEX day-ahead, intraday and TenneT imbalance, plus levies and kW-max tariffs). The ASIC band displaces boiler hours on cheap and negative-price hours, while the CHP keeps its high-temperature buffer, CO2 dosing and winter power sales. Heat is sold below the grower's gas-plus-ETS cost and Crossover keeps the hash; if the ASIC band can't beat a plain e-boiler, the optimiser becomes the product.
core_loop: Forecast heat demand, EPEX/imbalance prices and hashprice -> rolling 15-minute MILP assigns bands (ASICs on seconds-fast imbalance and cheap or negative hours, buffer over hours, boiler and CHP as the base) -> ASIC power targets set via firmware -> 55°C immersion heat feeds low-temperature circuits in place of boiler gas -> hash is paid out by an FPPS pool -> the grower is billed for heat below gas-plus-ETS cost.
why_now: Hashprice (~$28-30/PH/day) sits below miners' cash cost, so post-halving ASICs sell near scrap, and miners are being displaced by AI tenants (>$70B in AI/HPC contracts). Solar has made negative and volatile Dutch power prices routine. Netcongestie makes non-firm, leave-when-asked loads attractive to DSOs. Vertical farming's collapse (Infinite Acres, 80 Acres in 2026) showed that agriculture dies on energy cost, and the trends brief names a unified flexible-load market as the missing piece.
mvp: 90 days with one Westland grower. Weeks 1-4: two years of buffer, dispatch and heat-demand data, plus an all-in price model (EPEX plus levies plus kW-max tariffs) and a backtest of ASIC heat-plus-hash against boiler and e-boiler. Weeks 5-8: a 250 kW immersion ASIC pilot on a low-temperature loop with the optimiser in shadow mode. Weeks 9-12: live dispatch, with imbalance participation through the aggregator's BRP. Kill metric: if the ASIC band doesn't beat a plain e-boiler per MW-year after levies, tariffs and hardware failures, pivot to selling e-boiler and buffer controls.
stack: Pyomo/HiGHS rolling MILP on 15-minute imbalance settlement periods. EPEX day-ahead and intraday feeds and TenneT imbalance prices. Braiins OS/LuxOS firmware for ASIC power targets and curtailment, immersion tanks with plate heat exchangers, FPPS mining-pool payouts, and a read-only Priva/Hoogendoorn climate-computer integration.
business_model: Heat-as-a-service: Crossover owns the rigs, sells heat below the grower's gas-plus-ETS boiler cost, and keeps the hash revenue. Later, it licenses the optimiser to greenhouse energy aggregators, with a fallback of selling e-boiler and buffer controls if the ASIC band underperforms.
risks: A plain e-boiler may beat ASICs per MW-year once levies, tariffs and failure rates are counted (the kill metric)
Grid connection capacity (netcongestie) is scarce, and each MW competes with the grower's own electrification
Kilowatt-hour levies and kW-max tariffs can erase negative wholesale prices
Seasonal mismatch: summer heat has little value, so ASICs run hash-only and dump heat; ATES charging is not viable at the 25°C permit cap
Temperature mismatch: 55°C immersion heat fits only low-temperature circuits, not 90°C CHP buffers
Hashprice collapse and the 2028 halving; old-rig failure rates; immersion-fluid fire safety
REMIT market-manipulation exposure when chasing imbalance prices
Bitcoin's reputation and greenwashing risk; never claim carbon negative
moonshot: One connection, many bands. Connections, not electrons, become the scarce resource, and DSOs grant capacity by band: firm for GPUs and climate control, non-firm for sponges, seconds-fast for batteries. Mixed-load campuses share one connection and clear power and heat in a local auction. The greenhouse becomes the compute economy's retirement home: dying ASICs, retired GPUs running deferrable batch jobs and second-life EV packs, each valued as an option on volatility, not on spec.
best_line: Hashing is the only product here that travels for free, so heat demand picks the site and the hashes go out over fibre.
